section_summary: This section follows 1948 efforts to restore Allied patent and trademark rights in Japan, clarify wartime losses, and set occupation policy for the Japanese Patent Office. It includes business inquiries, State Department replies, Far Eastern Commission proposals, SCAP directives on patent licensing and secret patents, and a directive affecting trademarks associated with former industrial combines. Page 291 concludes an earlier discussion of Japanese copyright law and its treaty relationship with the United States.

subfiles.title: Discussion of Japanese copyright law and international relations
subfiles.about: Continues an account of copyright permissions, protection of foreign works, and the 1905 United States–Japan treaty.
subfiles.summary: Explains copyright licensing when owners cannot be located and treaty treatment of works and translations.

subfiles.title: Request for a draft Japanese patent law
subfiles.about: Asks whether a draft patent law for Japan is available to the Council’s patent committee.
subfiles.summary: Requests copies of any draft Japanese patent law.

subfiles.title: Reply to Behr on Japanese patent legislation
subfiles.about: Explains that no draft law is being prepared in Washington and invites proposed changes to existing law.
subfiles.summary: Says Japanese legislation is prepared under SCAP direction and welcomes the committee’s suggestions.

subfiles.title: International General Electric inquiry on patent policy
subfiles.about: Seeks patent policy information relevant to a possible new licensing agreement with Tokyo Shibaura.
subfiles.summary: Asks about expected patent law changes and conditions for renewing electrical engineering licensing.

subfiles.title: Reply on Tokyo Shibaura licensing and patent policy
subfiles.about: Discusses limited anticipated patent revisions and legal constraints on a new Tokyo Shibaura agreement.
subfiles.summary: Says United States policy chiefly seeks equitable restoration of wartime losses. Discusses Japanese antimonopoly law, compulsory licensing, and possible deconcentration of Tokyo Shibaura.

subfiles.title: Handwritten routing note
subfiles.about: Routes a matter for discussion with colleagues, including Vernon.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten instruction concerning internal discussion; much of the text is illegible.

subfiles.title: Army message on secret Japanese patents
subfiles.about: Requests a security assessment before deciding whether secret Japanese patents should be published.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether any existing secret patents could seriously affect United States national security.

subfiles.title: United Engineering inquiry about Japanese and Manchukuo patents
subfiles.about: Seeks the status and possible recovery of company patents and applications held before the war.
subfiles.summary: Requests advice on seized Japanese rights and uncertain Manchukuo rights.

subfiles.title: Reply to United Engineering on prewar patents
subfiles.about: Reports planned Japanese patent restoration and the lack of information on Manchurian rights.
subfiles.summary: Anticipates a public restoration procedure but offers little prospect of recovering Manchurian patents.

subfiles.title: SANACC amendment covering registered designs
subfiles.about: Proposes including registered industrial designs within a Japanese patent policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that the paper covers registered utility models and designs, while excluding trademarks and copyrights.

subfiles.title: Brady’s transmittal of NFTC meeting report
subfiles.about: Sends a draft account of the April 21 patent meeting for State Department corrections.
subfiles.summary: Requests corrections before distributing the meeting report to NFTC committees.

subfiles.title: Draft report of April 21 NFTC–State Department meeting
subfiles.about: Records discussion of Japanese Patent Office operations, restoration of Allied rights, and possible legal changes.
subfiles.summary: The draft says Japan’s prewar patent law remains in force and only limited changes are contemplated. It outlines restoration and extensions for Allied owners, discusses licensing and royalties, and records NFTC criticisms of penalties, opposition proceedings, annual fees, and working requirements.

subfiles.title: Second copy of April 21 meeting report
subfiles.about: Repeats the NFTC account of its meeting with State Department representatives.
subfiles.summary: This copy restates the draft’s proposed treatment of Allied patents and NFTC’s concerns about Japanese patent law. Its text contains minor transcription differences.

subfiles.title: Claxton corrections to NFTC meeting report
subfiles.about: Corrects the proposed public account of patent restoration policy and application procedures.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that Japanese nationals may already file applications, back wartime fees would not be due, and foreign owners should apply directly to SCAP. It distinguishes patent policy from licensing agreements and corrects wording on trademarks and the Italian treaty annex.

subfiles.title: Hooker Electrochemical patent status inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks what happened to Japanese Patent No. 104,290 and how Hooker can protect its rights.
subfiles.summary: Seeks information on vesting, licensing, blocked funds, renewal, and term extension.

subfiles.title: Interim reply on Hooker patent
subfiles.about: Reports that occupation authorities have been asked to investigate Hooker’s patent.
subfiles.summary: Promises findings and supplies general information on patent extensions and return of blocked property.

subfiles.title: Request to restitution delegation on Hooker patent
subfiles.to: Chief, United States Reparations and Restitution Delegation
subfiles.about: Requests facts about the Hooker patent’s status, wartime disposition, and blocked account.
subfiles.summary: Directs the Tokyo delegation to investigate the first three questions in Rose’s letter.

subfiles.title: Acheson Colloids trademark inquiry
subfiles.about: Lists Acheson’s Oildag, Aquadag, and dag registrations and asks whether renewals are needed.
subfiles.summary: Requests present status and steps to preserve six Japanese trademark registrations.

subfiles.title: Reply on Acheson trademark rights
subfiles.about: Explains planned procedures for restoring and revalidating foreign trademarks.
subfiles.summary: Says a public announcement is expected and no immediate action is necessary.

subfiles.title: Brief on SANACC 369/1 Japanese patent policy
subfiles.about: Summarizes the proposed United States policy for Japanese and foreign patent rights.
subfiles.summary: The brief recommends approval of restoration, term extensions, pending application reinstatement, and rules for secret patents and Japanese owned rights abroad. It notes SCAP discretion over patent uses needed for occupation objectives and pending military clearance.

subfiles.title: Martin inquiry about manufacturing in Japan
subfiles.about: Asks whether a Japanese manufacturer could make his patented meter chart calculator.
subfiles.summary: Seeks permission guidance and a possible Japanese manufacturing contact.

subfiles.title: Reply to Martin on Japanese manufacturing arrangements
subfiles.about: Explains SCAP licensing and the importance of a proposal’s foreign exchange effect.
subfiles.summary: Directs Martin to apply to SCAP. It says arrangements yielding net payments to Japan are more likely to be approved and anticipates future procedural changes.

subfiles.title: Tokyo report on Hooker patent and royalties
subfiles.about: Reports the cancellation, wartime licensing, and blocked royalties associated with Hooker patents.
subfiles.summary: Patent No. 104290 was cancelled for unpaid fees; a Bank of Japan account held ¥10,992.95 in royalties.

subfiles.title: Final reply to Rose on Hooker patent
subfiles.about: Passes on the Tokyo delegation’s findings concerning Hooker’s patent and blocked account.
subfiles.summary: Reports cancellation in 1942, wartime licenses, and ¥10,992.95 deposited in a blocked account.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting SCAPIN 1902
subfiles.about: Transmits a directive allowing licensing of nonsecret Japanese government patents.
subfiles.summary: Explains that licensing is permitted to support economic rehabilitation; a secret patent directive may follow.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1902: Licensing of Government-Owned Patents
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Authorizes nonexclusive licensing of government patents and utility models except those formerly declared secret.
subfiles.summary: Requires reasonable royalties, nondiscrimination, and periodic reports identifying each license and royalty terms.

subfiles.title: International Standard Electric patent ownership claim
subfiles.to: Office of the Legal Adviser, Department of State
subfiles.about: Asserts beneficial ownership of inventions patented in Nippon Electric’s name under prewar agreements.
subfiles.summary: Phinney explains contract terms requiring eventual assignment of patents derived from International Standard Electric inventions. He promises evidence and a list of affected patents and requests their transfer.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to International Standard Electric
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the company’s claimed interest in patents held by Nippon Electric.
subfiles.summary: Invites additional supporting information.

subfiles.title: Army concurrence with SANACC patent proposals
subfiles.about: States Army agreement with the substance of proposed Japanese patent policy.
subfiles.summary: Offers to treat the proposals as agreed United States policy and inform MacArthur and the FEC representative.

subfiles.title: Lewis memorandum on delayed Army patent clearance
subfiles.about: Explains delays in Army clearance of FEC patent and utility model papers.
subfiles.summary: Reports that the secret patent objection had fallen away but formal Army approval remained stalled.

subfiles.title: FEC C1-284/3 transmittal note
subfiles.about: Circulates a proposed policy for patents and utility models in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Introduces the subcommittee’s enclosure and records its scope and membership.

subfiles.title: FEC policy toward patents and utility models in Japan
subfiles.about: Proposes occupation policy for the Patent Office and Allied patent rights in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Calls for publication of secret patents, restoration of Allied rights, waiver of wartime fees, and reinstatement of pending applications. It offers owners a choice involving term extension and wartime royalties, protects certain priority claims, and allows intervention where patent rights obstruct occupation purposes.

subfiles.title: FEC C1-311 transmittal note
subfiles.about: Circulates recommendations on Japanese owned patent rights in United Nations territories.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the Patents Subcommittee report and its participating delegations.

subfiles.title: Recommendations on Japanese owned patents abroad
subfiles.about: Recommends treatment of Japanese patents, utility models, and designs held in former enemy countries.
subfiles.summary: Urges public availability of vested rights while protecting lawful third party interests and permitting certain postwar Japanese applications.

subfiles.title: Instruction to United States FEC representative
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Authorizes agreement in the FEC following approval of SANACC 369/1.
subfiles.summary: Conveys approved United States patent policy with a qualification concerning international trade and imports.

subfiles.title: State Department concurrence to Royall
subfiles.about: Confirms joint State and Army treatment of SANACC patent proposals as occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: Says the FEC member has been advised and concurs in informing MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Informal patent answers sent to French delegation
subfiles.about: Sends informal answers to questions about Japanese patents.
subfiles.summary: Transmits an answer memorandum that is not present in this section.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting secret patent directive
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP’s order to reclassify formerly secret patents and utility models.
subfiles.summary: Notes that government owned rights may be licensed unless they concern weapons or means of war.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1902/1: Reclassification of Secret Patents
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Ends secret classification of patents, utility models, and pending applications.
subfiles.summary: Orders ordinary treatment and permits licensing of eligible government owned rights.

subfiles.title: Swiss note on wartime damage claims
subfiles.about: Requests the procedure for Swiss citizens’ war damage claims against Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks where claims should be filed after occupation authorities declined competence.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Swiss representatives on claims and patents
subfiles.from: Roger C. Dixon and Michael J. Dux
subfiles.about: Records advice on Swiss wartime claims and Geigy’s Japanese penicillin patent royalties.
subfiles.summary: State officials advise that Swiss claims await FEC policy and should be presented through SCAP. They describe prospective restoration of foreign patents, possible payment of royalties in yen, and uncertainty over any advance payment to Geigy.

subfiles.title: Despatch on SCAP trademark and trade name directive
subfiles.about: Explains SCAP’s plan to prevent successor companies from retaining marks of dissolved industrial combines.
subfiles.summary: The directive would allow injunctions against common zaibatsu marks and make barred marks freely usable. The despatch notes concern that unrestricted use could mislead the public.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1923: Trademarks and names of designated combines
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Orders changes to Japanese law governing marks shared by holding companies, affiliates, and excessive concentrations.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes the Holding Company Liquidation Commission to cancel or enjoin specified marks and names, including listed zaibatsu names. It requires legislation barring future exclusive registration of enjoined marks and interim implementation by Cabinet order.

subfiles.title: NFTC request for industrial property meeting
subfiles.about: Requests discussion of NFTC proposals for restoring American industrial property rights in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Loree urges prompt return of patents and trademarks and restoration of the Japanese patent system. He encloses detailed proposals and requests a meeting with State Department officials.

subfiles.title: NFTC proposals on Japanese industrial property
subfiles.about: Sets out proposed protections for United States patents, trademarks, and marks of origin in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Council seeks restoration, term extensions, fee waivers, infringement remedies, and priority rights. It proposes changes to Japanese patent penalties, opposition, annual taxes, and working rules, plus trademark protection and clear country of origin marking.

subfiles.title: Saltzman reply arranging NFTC meeting
subfiles.about: Accepts a meeting to discuss NFTC industrial property proposals.
subfiles.summary: Invites Bradley to arrange a mutually convenient time.
